Implementing security measures such as authentication tokens, HTTPS, and 
data storage encryption as the application has, is imperative to mitigating 
potential security breaches. 
The Freedom of Information Act 2000, ensures that the public can access their 
own information, understanding that students or their parents may request 
information about their data is critical (Metropolitan Police, n.d.). For this case 
data must be accessible and retrievable for these scenarios. 
The Information Systems Regulations 2018, cover security of networks and 
information systems which is vital for ensuring the general public’s activities, 
without uninvited disruption (UK Government, 2018). For this the application 
implements high security standards, such as authentication tokens and HTTPS 
communication protocols. 
6.3.2 Social Issues 
The integration of leader boards and completive elements that put scores onto 
students’ abilities may induce anxiety among students, and primarily among 
students that are already stressed in academic environments. To mitigate this 
leader boards are an opt-in feature, thereby allowing students to focus on their 
personal progress instead of comparing themselves to others. 
Another issue that may arise from leader boards is their tendency to induce self-
comparison, among students and their peers. While this feature is optional, its 
mere presents may pressure students into joining, which could affect the 
students’ self-esteem and motivation. To lower the likely hood of students 
experiencing this issue, students are placed into leader boards at random, and 
are ranked among students with a similar work ethic.
